scope.summary: Ordinary full-scope audit (compact team, workspace AGENTS.md 'Audit depth') of the uncommitted modular refactor on d7af4b1: Rust library, command-line tool, single-WASM bindings, the browser package (web/ and the local dist/ build), build and release scripts and workflows, documentation and audit records; verification of the six AUD-009 findings. Not release acceptance.
excluded: Canonical Docker rebuild and release archives; paid GitHub Actions runs.
Argon2 above 256 MiB in the reviewers' work; full-size runs only in the coordinator's capped chain, one at a time.
Cross-target compilation and runtime (aarch64-linux, windows-gnu, windows-msvc, macOS).
Upstream dependency internals and an independent cryptographic proof.
mhfe_spec and multi-chain-wallet-tools were read, not audited.
scope.counterpart: mhfe_spec read only as the counterpart specification (README sections cited in the findings); its working tree was at HEAD 2cd5e4c96a2bf2cc177f8b99b81fa7427bdf1b86 with local changes when this record was written; the reviewers did not record its state.
scope.environment: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64, 16 CPUs, 15.4 GB memory; rustc and Cargo 1.99.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129, Node 26.10.0, Python 3.14.4, Emscripten 6.0.10, Playwright 1.63.0 with Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and Firefox 155.0, cargo audit 0.22.2 with the local advisory database at ef6173cb (2026-10-03) (local-only environment.log and the reviewers' logs).
scope.methodology: A coverage planner assigned all 32 CHECK-* items of FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md; five reviewers worked in parallel on distinct scopes with source traces bound to file hashes, independent oracles written for the audit, production-source probes, pseudo-terminal probes and the shared check.sh and real-browser runs; each reviewer's findings went to a separate challenger who reproduced or re-derived them and confirmed, downgraded or refuted each one. All 24 findings were confirmed (one downgraded); none was refuted. Only public test vectors and synthetic secrets were used; reviewers edited no production, test, fixture, documentation or script file.

checks.title: Threat model and secret ownership
checks.methodAndLimits: Source trace of every secret's owning type, its copies from src/ through src/wasm_api/, the workers and the classes to the CLI, its lifetime, reveal and return paths and cleanup, with file hashes. wasm-residue.mjs W1 and W2 pass, W3 fails; client-lifecycle.mjs passes. No document promises a vault or claims the container holds the BIP39 passphrase; startup checks use public inputs only. Failed on SEC001 and SEC002. Limits: immutable JavaScript strings, freed WebAssembly memory, panic = abort, host compromise.

checks.title: Secret Vault, CSP, sandbox, and transport
checks.methodAndLimits: Vault and iframe part not applicable: a library package, whose host CSP belongs to the embedding page. Worker transport probed with production web/ and the real dist worker (75 passed, 5 failed): compiled-module hand-over, secret transfer, build handshake and refusal, late and duplicate replies, start failures, the one-minute start limit, unknown names and wiping pass; names inherited from Object.prototype are served (API002). The real-browser run used exactly the documented CSP in Chromium 153 and Firefox 155, both modes; no remote URL, import() or importScripts in any dist script.

checks.title: Network egress and secret guards
checks.methodAndLimits: cargo tree for native and wasm32 shows no network crate; network-scan.mjs finds no network or remote-loading API outside reviewed local-only uses and src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs; serve.rs loopback limits traced and unit-tested; cli-process-protection.py: core size 0, not dumpable, NoNewPrivs and seccomp on every thread and only 'lo' in the namespace while encrypt and decrypt --stdin wait. Secret-pattern tripwires not applicable (no public-input export boundary).

checks.title: Randomness, encryption, and authentication
checks.methodAndLimits: Randomness only from getrandom (CLI) and the worker's getRandomValues, each draw after a source health check, unbiased uniform_below, all-zero entropy refused; random-source.mjs R1 to R4 pass. Argon2id parameters, memory levels and password encoding traced; no authentication by design, as the specification states. Byte-level cipher correctness is under CHECK-FUN-006; Argon2 here at most the 256 MiB known answer.

checks.title: Secret lifecycle and exceptional paths
checks.methodAndLimits: client-lifecycle.mjs: every page copy of a secret is transferred or wiped on refused repetitions, start failures, cancellation, late answers and hidden-wallet sessions (the AUD-009-SEC001 and -API001 paths included), confirmed in Chromium and Firefox; Rust Drop and zeroize of Password, LockedText, RecoveredPhrase, round values and the work area traced; core dumps off before any secret. Failed on SEC003 (error-path unlock order) and SEC001 (phrase text in linear memory). Practical zeroization only.

checks.title: Browser injection, persistence, and sensitive APIs
checks.methodAndLimits: static-scan.mjs (14 passed): no DOM sink, storage, dynamic code, console call or network call in first-party scripts; console calls only in generated Emscripten and wasm-bindgen glue; error texts carry no phrase, password or passphrase; no page-loaded script names a coin or carries a wallet vector.

checks.title: Read-only guarantees and availability bounds
checks.methodAndLimits: Read-only part not applicable (no transaction, broadcast or spending surface). Availability bounds traced: 1,024-byte passwords, 8,192-byte CLI answers, word, repair and password sizes checked before allocation, search limits, memory levels checked before any secret, serve limits; errors, cancellation and failed self-checks never become success. Page-chosen unbounded inputs recorded as observations.

checks.title: BIP39, entropy, and seed interpretation
checks.methodAndLimits: Independent oracle (130 PASS): the BIP39 list hash, all 24 trezor vectors both ways with their seeds, leading-zero and all-0x00/0xFF entropies, the NFKD passphrase seed and BIP32 fingerprints. Library probe: 218 phrase readings and refusals, container facts and detection, master_fingerprint of every trezor phrase. The passphrase is never part of the container. Failed on FUN001 and API001.

checks.title: HD derivation and every coin/profile
checks.methodAndLimits: All 43 address known answers recomputed from scratch (own secp256k1, BIP32, Keccak-256, Bech32/Bech32m, CashAddr, Base58Check, BIP86 tweak) across every coin and profile, DIP-0017 and DIP-0018 vectors reproduced; 695 find_address requests over 24 roots, 59 address and path rules, highest indexes; coin required in the library and the browser. Limits: the CLI script default coin (UI006); a P2SH multisig address cannot be told from P2SH-P2WPKH.

findings.title: Phrases passed to the WebAssembly bindings as text stay unwiped in linear memory
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded documented-guarantee defect: the package's classes terminate the worker after each operation and the page already holds the phrase as an immutable JavaScript string.
affected: src/wasm_api/core.rs:119 (describePhrase, phrase: &str) and :264-265 (encrypt, phrase: &str)
src/wasm_api/wallet.rs:52 (walletCheck) and :61 (walletFingerprint)
Claims at src/wasm_api/mod.rs:12-15, docs/API.md:249-252 and docs/API.md:709-710
Browser build dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm (SHA-256 23b1fcecec69c077602ac40355676f243de0889c29ff0b7232e8dc24adb3a29b) and any program that uses the bindings directly
findings.reproduction: From the repository root: `docs/audits/AUD-010-harnesses/run-logged.sh secrets-security-wasm-residue node docs/audits/AUD-010-harnesses/secrets-security/wasm-residue.mjs`. The probe loads target/wasm-bindgen/mhfe.js over dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm in Node, one fresh instance per call, passes a public phrase typed in capitals with double spaces (the BIP39 vector 7f..7f and the abandon..about phrase) to describePhrase, walletFingerprint and encrypt (Argon2 rounds at 256 KiB and one pass; known answers at full cost through dist/core/argon2-st.js), and counts that typed form in the linear memory after the call returns.
findings.expected: Per src/wasm_api/mod.rs ('Secrets arrive as UTF-8 bytes and are wiped here after use') and docs/API.md:249 ('Every buffer and binding this crate owns that holds a password, phrase, ... is wiped when dropped'), no copy of a phrase stays in the module's memory once a binding returns, as is already the case for password and passphrase bytes, secret results and session secrets.
findings.observed: One copy of the typed phrase remains after each of the three calls (describePhrase, walletFingerprint, encrypt); all 23 other measurements (passwords, passphrases and dice digits as bytes, secret results, hidden-wallet and rekey sessions after free()) leave none. Cause: wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 copies a &str argument into the module heap and frees it through its anchor Box<str> (wasm-bindgen src/convert/slices.rs:463-470) without overwriting it; the phrase inputs are &str while passwords are Vec<u8> wrapped in SecretText.
findings.impact: The original phrase (encrypt, describePhrase) or a recovered phrase (walletCheck, walletFingerprint) stays readable in freed WebAssembly memory of the worker until the worker is terminated. The package's classes terminate it right after each operation (web/runtime.js:178-187), so the window is short there; a program that keeps one instance of the bindings alive, as docs/API.md describes for embedders, accumulates such copies. Requires read access to the worker's memory; no persistence or network exposure. A documented wiping guarantee is not met for phrases.

findings.title: Locked memory covers fewer phrase copies than SECURITY.md states
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Coverage gap of a best-effort protection; exposure needs an unencrypted swap device and later access to it, and the tool warns before any secret when swap is not encrypted.
affected: src/mhfe.rs:215-234 (Mhfe::encrypt_unchecked: the bip39 Mnemonic 'source', 'entropy' and the packed state 'x' live unlocked through rounds 1-12; x is locked only at line 234 after forward())

findings.reproduction: Source trace of `mhfe encrypt` and `mhfe check` on Linux with mlock permitted: the typed line (hidden_input.rs, LockedText) and Password are locked; in Mhfe::encrypt_unchecked, phrase::parse (215), the Zeroizing entropy (216) and the Zeroizing packed state x (217-224) are created unlocked and stay alive while Permutation::forward runs twelve Argon2 rounds (228-232) with the 2 GiB work area reserved; LockedPages::of_vec(&x) is called only at 234. In mhfe check, compare_state reads each candidate phrase with read_phrase into an unlocked Zeroizing<String> and searches addresses with it while the work area is still reserved. Besides LockedText the library calls LockedPages::of_* only at src/mhfe.rs:109, src/mhfe.rs:234 and src/password.rs:57.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:50-54: 'The password, the original phrase while it is encrypted, the entropy kept for the check, a recovered phrase, a BIP39 passphrase and the line a secret is typed into are locked in memory (mlock), so that the system does not write them to swap'.
findings.observed: Only the typed line, Password, the OriginalFacts words, the NewContainer source (after round 12), the RecoveredPhrase text and the passphrase copies held by HiddenWallets and PhraseDraw are locked. Phrase-equivalent working copies (entropy, packed state, Feistel halves, the bip39 Mnemonic word indexes, the rehearsal's recovered phrase text and state, the NFKD passphrase and the BIP39 seed) are wiped on drop but never locked.
findings.impact: While the multi-GiB Argon2 work area creates memory pressure for the one to two minutes of the rounds (hours at a high PIM), the kernel may write these small pages to an unencrypted swap device, where the phrase can outlast the program. Bounded: the protection is documented as best effort, the tool warns before any secret when swap is not encrypted, an attacker needs later access to the swap device, and the Argon2 area itself already allows cheap password testing there. Browser and Windows builds lock nothing by design.

findings.title: Error paths of Password::new and the hidden line editor unlock pages before wiping them
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A window of a few instructions on error paths only; native Unix only; no exposure demonstrated.
affected: src/password.rs:55-76 (Err(PasswordTooLong) at 71)
src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:341-379 (returns at 351, 355, 374 and 376-378, and the `?` returns of erase, write_all and flush)

findings.reproduction: Source trace by Rust drop order (locals drop in reverse order of declaration). Password::new declares 'encoded' (55) before its guard 'locked' (57); on a password over 1,024 bytes after NFKD the function returns Err with both still local, so the guard drops first (pages::release, munlock) and 'encoded', holding the first 1,024 normalized bytes, is zeroized afterwards. edit_line declares 'line' (341) before 'line_locked' (343); an answer longer than 8,192 bytes (376-378), a read error (355), or Ctrl+D on an empty line after Ctrl+U left typed bytes in the spare capacity (374, 351) return early and unlock the buffer before Zeroizing wipes it. The success paths are correct: LockedText and Password keep the guard as a field after the buffer.
findings.expected: src/memory.rs:19 and src/password.rs:29 ('pages are unlocked only once they are wiped') and SECURITY.md:53 ('a typed line stays locked until it is wiped').
findings.observed: On those error paths the pages are unlocked a few instructions before the secret bytes on them are overwritten.
findings.impact: A window of microseconds in which up to 8 KiB of a typed secret, or 1 KiB of a normalized password, lies on unlocked pages; swapping in that window is unlikely. A defect against a stated invariant rather than a demonstrated exposure. AUD-009 noted the same pattern for password generation, which LockedText::build now fixes.
